summary: This lecture tells of the rebuilding of the Kaaba when the Prophet SAW was 35. The ustaz recalls ten years of his life with Khadijah in a large house full of people he helped. Floods that kept damaging the Kaaba and thefts led Quraysh to gather clean funds to rebuild it, and a Roman ship wrecked at Jeddah supplied timber and stone and an architect named Bakum. Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah bravely began the demolition. A dispute over who would place the Black Stone nearly led to bloodshed, but the Prophet SAW, the first to walk through the door, settled it by placing the stone on a cloth held by all the tribes. The ustaz also explains the history of the Black Stone and the story of Zaid ibn Amr ibn Nufail, who rejected idols before prophethood.
keyPoints: The household of the Prophet SAW and Khadijah held about fifteen people, and he set up a green tent giving food and clothes to the poor.
The Kaaba was rebuilt because of floods and theft, with funds from clean sources only and timber and stone from a wrecked Roman ship.
A five-day dispute over placing the Black Stone was settled by the Prophet SAW, Al-Amin, with a cloth held by all the tribes.
The Black Stone came down from paradise white and turned black because of the sins of the children of Adam.
Zaid ibn Amr ibn Nufail rejected idols and saved baby girls, and the Prophet SAW said he received two levels of paradise.

chapters.title: Opening
chapters.summary: The ustaz gives thanks for health and prays for pupils who are unwell.

chapters.title: Recap and ten quiet years
chapters.summary: The ustaz recalls Zaid ibn Harithah and says he stayed focused on family and trade from 25 to 35.

chapters.title: A large house and the green tent
chapters.summary: About fifteen people lived in his house, and a green tent outside gave free food and clothing to the poor.

chapters.title: The old Kaaba and the floods
chapters.summary: The old Kaaba had no roof and was low, lying in a valley that often flooded and was a target for thieves.

chapters.title: Clean funds and the Roman ship
chapters.summary: Quraysh accepted only clean money, but funds fell short until a Roman ship wrecked at Jeddah and its timber and stone were bought.

chapters.title: Al-Walid begins the demolition
chapters.summary: Everyone was afraid, but Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah began with an axe and prayed not to be punished.

chapters.title: The building and the architect Bakum
chapters.summary: Each tribe got a section, and the architect Bakum reshaped the Kaaba into a rectangle with the Hijr Ismail, a roof, drainage and a raised door.

chapters.title: The dispute over the Black Stone
chapters.summary: Each tribe wanted to place the Black Stone and they quarrelled for five days, nearly killing each other.

chapters.title: Abu Umayyah's proposal
chapters.summary: The eldest, Abu Umayyah, proposed that the first person to enter the door next day decide.

chapters.title: Muhammad Al-Amin
chapters.summary: The 35-year-old Prophet SAW was the first to enter, and all were glad because he was Al-Amin.

chapters.title: The cloth and the Black Stone
chapters.summary: He placed the stone on his cloth, all the tribes lifted it, and he set it in its place.

chapters.title: The foundation of Adam and Ibrahim
chapters.summary: As they dug down they reached the foundation stone from Prophet Adam's time, where Prophet Ibrahim built.

chapters.title: The history of the Black Stone
chapters.summary: The stone came from paradise, whiter than milk, and turned black because of sin. The ustaz advises not to hurt people to kiss it.

chapters.title: Zaid ibn Amr ibn Nufail
chapters.summary: Before revelation he rejected idols, stopped the burying of baby girls and sought the prophet, but was killed by robbers.

chapters.title: Zaid's reward and closing
chapters.summary: His son Said embraced Islam and the Prophet SAW said Zaid received two levels of paradise. The ustaz closes the series on life before prophethood.

dalil.context: The ustaz recites the verse about Prophet Ibrahim raising the foundations of the Kaaba.
dalil.translation: As Abraham and Ishmael built up the foundations of the House [they prayed], ‘Our Lord, accept [this] from us. You are the All Hearing, the All Knowing.
The Prophet SAW said the Black Stone came down from paradise, whiter than milk, then turned black from the sins of the children of Adam.
dalil.context: The ustaz relates the Prophet's words. He does not name a narrator or source.

dalil.translation: By Allah, Allah will raise the stone on the Day of Judgement with two eyes that see and a tongue that speaks, testifying for whoever touched it.
dalil.context: The ustaz mentions this hadith when explaining the merit of kissing the Black Stone.

dalil.translation: When asked about Zaid ibn Amr, the Prophet SAW said he received two levels in paradise.
dalil.context: The ustaz relates the Prophet's answer to Said ibn Zaid. He does not name a source.

books.context: A sirah summary covering the rebuilding of the Kaaba and the Prophet's role.

Lived with her baby Aiman in his house.

sirah.summary: This lecture covers his life from 25 to 35, the rebuilding of the Kaaba, the history of the Black Stone and the story of Zaid ibn Amr.

events.label: Flood
events.title: A flood damages the Kaaba
events.desc: A great flood and thefts made Quraysh realise the Kaaba needed rebuilding.

events.label: Ship
events.title: A Roman ship is wrecked at Jeddah
events.desc: Timber and stone meant for a church in Yemen were sold to Quraysh.

events.label: Al-Walid
events.title: Al-Walid starts demolishing
events.desc: He volunteered and the others waited a day before continuing.

events.label: Bakum
events.title: Bakum redesigns the Kaaba
events.desc: The Kaaba was built as a rectangle with the Hijr Ismail and a roof.

events.label: Quarrel
events.title: The quarrel over the Black Stone
events.desc: The project halted for five days as the tribes quarrelled.

events.label: Proposal
events.title: Abu Umayyah proposes a solution
events.desc: The first to enter the door next morning would decide.

events.label: Al-Amin
events.title: The Prophet SAW enters first
events.desc: All were glad because he was Al-Amin and accepted his decision.

events.label: Cloth
events.title: The Black Stone is placed on a cloth
events.desc: Each tribe held the cloth and the Prophet SAW set the stone.

lessons.title: Clean funds for Allah's house
lessons.body: Quraysh accepted only money from clean sources, not from wine, theft or fraud.

lessons.title: Helping the poor
lessons.body: The Prophet SAW gave free food and clothes to those in need, like food banks at mosques today.

lessons.title: Courage to start a great task
lessons.body: Al-Walid volunteered to begin the demolition though everyone was afraid.

lessons.title: Praying while doing good
lessons.body: Al-Walid prayed that Allah not punish them since they were repairing His house.

lessons.title: Not fighting to the point of killing
lessons.body: They fought almost to killing while building the house of God.

lessons.title: Honesty earns trust
lessons.body: All the tribes accepted Muhammad as judge because he was Al-Amin, the most honest.

lessons.title: A solution that involves everyone
lessons.body: With the cloth, the Prophet SAW gave every tribe an equal share.

lessons.title: Kissing the Black Stone without harming
lessons.body: We love the sunnah of kissing it but must not hurt or pull others' clothing.

lessons.title: Seeking the truth
lessons.body: Zaid ibn Amr rejected idols and said they did not follow the religion of Ibrahim.

lessons.title: Saving lives
lessons.body: Zaid ibn Amr redeemed baby girls about to be buried alive.
